content:
The image shows a stem near the soil line with:
- White cotton-like mycelium covering the infected stem tissue
- Multiple dark grayish-black sclerotia (hard resting structures) embedded within the white mycelium
- Bleached, dried stem tissue at the infection site

Key diagnostic reasoning:
- The white cottony mycelium + dark sclerotia combination is the hallmark of fungal stem rot diseases
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: sclerotia are grayish-black, grain-of-rice sized — matches the image well
- **Southern_Blight**: sclerotia are mustard-seed sized, more numerous, range from tan to reddish-brown to black — the sclerotia in this image appear larger and fewer, more consistent with Sclerotinia

The sclerotia visible here are dark gray-black, relatively large (grain of rice), and few in number, embedded in white mycelium on the stem. This matches the Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot description precisely.
